excerpts.text: For example, a CONNECT request ([Section 9.3.6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9110/#CONNECT)) or a request with the Upgrade header field ([Section 7.8](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9110/#field.upgrade)) can occur at any time, not just in the first message on a connection.
Once active, a tunnel is not considered a party to the HTTP communication, though the tunnel might have been initiated by an HTTP request.

Tunnels are used to extend a virtual connection through an intermediary, such as when Transport Layer Security (TLS, [[TLS13](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9110/#TLS13)]) is used to establish confidential communication through a shared firewall proxy.[¶](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9110/#section-3.7-8)

| CONNECT | Establish a tunnel to the server named by the target | no | no |
| TRACE | Message loop back test along the path | yes | yes |

> "The TRACE method requests a remote, application-level loop-back of the request message. The final recipient of the request SHOULD reflect the message received, excluding some fields described below, back to the client as the content of a 200 (OK) response." -- RFC 9110 §9.3.8
